rows.title: 3.4L V6 Intake Manifold and Head Gasket Coolant Leaks (Dex-Cool)
rows.howToFix: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with updated Fel-Pro 'Problem Solver' metal-carrier gaskets and perform a full cooling system flush. If the engine overheated, have the heads checked for warpage and replace head gaskets as needed. Service Dex-Cool on time and never let the system run low.

rows.title: 4T65-E Transmission Failure and Pressure Control Solenoid Erratic Shifting
rows.howToFix: Diagnose stored codes first: P1811 with harsh shifts points to the pressure control solenoid, which requires removing the transmission side cover (engine cradle lowered) to replace. Severely slipping or non-driving units need a rebuilt or remanufactured 4T65-E. Fluid and filter service every 50,000 miles extends solenoid and clutch life.

rows.title: Erratic Fuel Gauge from Failed Fuel Level Sensor
rows.howToFix: Replace the fuel level sensor/sending unit, which on the Aztek requires dropping the fuel tank to access the pump module — many shops recommend replacing the complete pump module at the same time given the labor overlap. Inspect and clean the sender connector and wiring for corrosion before condemning the sender.

rows.title: Instrument Cluster Stepper Motor Failure — Stuck, Pegged, or Erratic Gauges
rows.howToFix: Repair rather than replace: install updated Switec X27.168 stepper motors (the GM-authorized replacement), renew the backlight bulbs, and reflow the cracked solder joints. Mail-in cluster rebuild services do all of this with a warranty; handy DIYers can replace the motors with a soldering iron for under $100 in parts.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Aztek/Rendezvous Intermediate Steering Shaft — 2003 Recall + General Clunk Issue

General clunk: disassemble the intermediate shaft, clean and re-lube splines with synthetic grease (DIY) or pay ~$80 shop labor. If splines are visibly worn, replace the shaft ($150-$300 part). GM "shaft lube kit" with snap-in collar is a durable fix.

rows.title: Premature Front Wheel Hub Bearing Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the failed hub/bearing assembly with a quality (preferably OE-grade) unit, torque the axle nut to spec, and clean the integrated wheel speed sensor connector to clear ABS/AWD warnings. Inspect both sides — owners frequently report sequential failure of the opposite hub.

rows.title: Rear Liftgate Electronic Release Failure — Hatch Will Not Open
rows.howToFix: Replace the failed liftgate latch/release actuator (accessed by removing the interior hatch trim and manually tripping the latch with a screwdriver while an assistant pulls the gate). Check the release circuit fuse and wiring first, and replace both gas struts if the hatch will not stay up.

rows.title: Versatrak AWD Rear Differential Failure — AWD Disable Light and Clutch Chatter
rows.howToFix: Change the Versatrak rear differential fluid with the correct GM fluid every 15,000-30,000 miles — early fluid service cures most chatter and groaning. Fix seal leaks promptly; once the clutch pumps or check valves fail, the accepted repair is a rebuilt or good used rear carrier assembly (GM part 88894200 era).

rows.howToFix: Test the crank sensor and ICM circuits and replace the failed component; the dual CKP sensor sits behind the harmonic balancer, so the crank pulley must be pulled, and a crank relearn may be required after replacement. Many high-mileage owners replace the CKP sensor and ICM together to end repeat intermittent stalls.

rows.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge (Stepper Motor) and Backlighting Failure
rows.howToFix: Have the cluster rebuilt with updated X27.168-style stepper motors and new backlighting bulbs (mail-in services run about $130-$250 and preserve the odometer mileage), or replace the faulty stepper motors yourself with basic soldering skills. rows.title: Power Window Regulator Cable and Motor Failure

rows.title: Fuel Tank Pressure Sensor Defect — Fuel Leak and Fire Risk (NHTSA Recall 03V238000, SSEi)

If fuel odor or leakage is present, stop refueling, shut the vehicle off away from ignition sources, do not restart it, and arrange qualified inspection. The campaign remedy is dealer replacement of the fuel-tank pressure sensor; current availability and any charge for a vehicle of this age must be confirmed with GM rather than promised here. Do not buy a pressure sensor or other EVAP/fuel-system part from this page; recall eligibility, leak condition, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: 700-R4/4L60E Automatic Transmission 3-4 Clutch Pack Failure
rows.howToFix: A quality rebuild that addresses the root cause — Sonnax/TransGo corrective parts, upgraded 3-4 clutch pack and band, and verification of proper line-pressure rise — is the accepted fix. Replacement motors are also available; verify wiring, fuses, and grounds first by checking whether the manual knob on the motor spins when the switch is operated.

rows.title: Power Window Motor and Regulator Failure (Slow or Stuck Windows)
rows.howToFix: Replace the failed window motor (and regulator if the cable/sector gear is worn), drilling out the factory rivets and converting to bolts for easier future service. Annual lubrication of the window tracks and addressing the passenger-door power-feed voltage drop extend motor life.

rows.title: T-Top Water Leaks from Deteriorated Weatherstripping
rows.howToFix: Clean and recondition marginal seals with silicone/dielectric weatherstrip grease (GM 12345579) and adjust the door glass for firm seal contact; brittle or cracked weatherstrip must be replaced with a full reproduction seal kit. Persistent leaks at the windshield header may require removing trim and re-sealing with urethane adhesive.

rows.title: VATS/PassKey Anti-Theft System No-Start (Security Light, Car Won't Crank or Stalls)
rows.howToFix: Replace the worn key and/or ignition lock cylinder, or repair the broken pellet-sensing wires in the column. The widely accepted permanent fix on these aging cars is a resistor bypass matching one of GM's 15 pellet values (or a bypass module) wired into the VATS sensing circuit, a procedure extensively documented on F-body forums.

rows.title: 3.4L V6 Intake Manifold and Head Gasket Coolant Leaks (1993-1995)
rows.howToFix: Replace the intake manifold gaskets with updated steel-core Fel-Pro gaskets after pressure-testing to confirm the leak source; if combustion gases are present in the coolant, the head gasket must be replaced as well. Flush the cooling system and maintain fresh coolant to slow gasket deterioration.

rows.title: Rocker Panel and Lower Door Rust-Through
rows.howToFix: Catch early: grind to bare metal, treat with rust converter, prime and topcoat. Advanced cases require cut-and-weld rocker patch panels ($200 per side in parts, ~$1000 body-shop labor). GM's 6-year/100k corrosion warranty has long expired on these vehicles.

rows.title: StabiliTrak / Traction Control / ABS Warning from BCM Connector Corrosion
rows.howToFix: Remove the passenger kick panel to access the three large BCM connectors (especially the C2 connector); unlatch via the plastic levers, inspect for green/fretting corrosion, clean with electrical contact cleaner, apply dielectric grease per GM procedure (one-inch nylon bristle brush on C2 pins), and re-seat several times. Note: the 'Reduced Engine Power' message specifically is often caused by a separate IP-to-body harness connector in the DRIVER-side (left) kick panel carrying the APP signal — inspect both sides. Do NOT replace the BCM for this condition. Also scan wheel-speed and steering-position sensors before condemning the BCM.

rows.title: Ignition Switch May Slip Out of Run Position (Recall 14V400000)
rows.howToFix: Until the campaign remedy is confirmed complete, remove all other items and the key fob from the ignition-key ring as NHTSA directs. Check VIN/open-campaign status and ask the dealer to confirm current remedy availability and any charge in 2026. Diagnose separate switch/cylinder complaints independently. Do not buy an ignition switch, lock cylinder, key insert or cover from this page; campaign status, key configuration, failed path, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

Diagnose separate switch/cylinder complaints independently.

rows.title: Headlamp Driver Module (HDM) Overheat - Low Beams Fail (Recall 15V519000)
rows.howToFix: Have the HDM replaced free of charge under recall 15V519000 (GM recall 14291); 2006 models may be covered under GM's extended warranty program. Verify by VIN at NHTSA and address promptly given the safety impact.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Verify by VIN at NHTSA and address promptly given the safety impact.

rows.title: Front Strut-to-Tire Rub Destroying Inner Front Tire Sidewalls
rows.howToFix: Replace the front strut upper mounts, bearings, and radius rod bushings (Pedders or Whiteline urethane parts are the accepted fix), install eccentric camber/caster bolts, and realign to gain at least 1/4 inch of tire-to-strut clearance. Inspect inner front sidewalls regularly and replace any tire showing cord; alignment alone without the bushing/mount work rarely cures it.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Inspect inner front sidewalls regularly and replace any tire showing cord;

rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Ignition Lock Cylinder/Housing Binding — Key Will Not Turn
rows.howToFix: Replace the ignition lock housing with the revised-design GM part (the original barrel and key tumblers can be reused, so no re-coding is needed). As a temporary measure, rocking the steering wheel firmly while turning the key, or depressing the lock barrel into the housing, can relieve pin pressure enough to start the car.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Instrument Cluster LCD Odometer Pixel/Display Failure
rows.howToFix: Send the cluster to an instrument-cluster repair service for LCD replacement and solder re-flow of the power supply circuit, or fit a used cluster ($75-100) and have the mileage professionally reprogrammed to match the car. Simple resoldering fixes intermittent displays in some cases.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Internal Clutch Slave Cylinder / Throwout Bearing Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the slave cylinder/release bearing with a fresh GM unit (forum consensus is OEM over aftermarket), and replace it preventively any time the transmission is out for clutch work. Adding a remote bleeder line and an aluminum billet bearing support while in there are widely accepted upgrades.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Rear Differential Mount Bushing Deterioration — Driveline Clunk and Wheel Hop
rows.howToFix: Install a polyurethane differential mount insert (Whiteline or Pedders, roughly $40 in parts) to take up the slack in the factory bushing and restore pinion angle; replace the full mount and rear crossmember bushings if badly degraded. Check driveshaft-to-diff bolt torque whenever clunking appears.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Check driveshaft-to-diff bolt torque whenever clunking appears.

rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Rear Shock Upper (Pedestal) Mount Bushing Wear — Rear-End Clunk
rows.howToFix: Inspect the upper bushings by pulling back the trunk carpet over the tank sides; replace worn bushings with an uprated set (Whiteline W31467 kit, about $34) and torque the upper mount with the car on the ground, top first. If bushings are intact, properly re-torquing the upper and lower mounts cures most shock-sourced clunks.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Inspect the upper bushings by pulling back the trunk carpet over the tank sides;

rows.title: GTO LS2 Rear Tire Rub Under Hard Cornering
rows.howToFix: Inspect rear inner fender liner for cut marks at each tire rotation. Roll the rear fender lips ($150-$300 specialist) and trim back the plastic splash guard. Avoid maxing out cargo + passengers simultaneously. Aftermarket shorter springs without other geometry changes makes the rub WORSE, not better.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Inspect rear inner fender liner for cut marks at each tire rotation.

rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Power Sliding Door Can Open While Vehicle Is Moving (NHTSA Recall)
rows.howToFix: If the passenger-side power sliding door does not positively latch, keep occupants away from it and do not drive until secured and inspected. Check the VIN and campaign-completion history for 01V067 and 01V264 with NHTSA and a GM dealer. Ask the dealer to confirm the currently available inspection/remedy and any charge; do not infer present-day no-cost service from the historical owner letter. Do not buy an actuator or latch part from this page; campaign applicability, prior repair, installed assembly, part number and VIN fitment must be verified first.

rows.title: Montana 3.4L V6 Intake Gasket — Same as Grand Am
rows.howToFix: Same fix — updated Fel-Pro MS98010T LIM gasket + UIM gasket + plenum repair/replacement. $500-$1,000 at independent (minivan labor slightly higher due to packaging). Drain Dex-Cool, refill with Zerex G-05.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: 3.4L (3400) Lower Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant/Oil Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets, ideally with the updated Fel-Pro/aluminum-frame gasket set rather than the original plastic-carrier design. Inspect for coolant in the oil; if present, do an oil change immediately after the repair and check bearing condition. Many shops also resurface/clean the mating surfaces and replace the thermostat and coolant while the manifold is off.

if present, do an oil change immediately after the repair and check bearing condition.

rows.title: 4T65E Automatic Transmission Failure (Slipping, Shudder, Hard Shifts)
rows.howToFix: Service fluid and filter on schedule; many owners/specialists add an auxiliary transmission cooler to combat heat-related failure. For slipping or shudder, diagnose pressure and solenoid operation first; a worn unit typically requires a rebuild or a remanufactured 4T65E. Address any external leaks (axle seals, side cover) promptly to avoid running low.

rows.title: Blower Motor / HVAC Blower Resistor Failure
rows.howToFix: If only high speed works, replace the blower motor resistor (located near the blower motor, usually accessible behind dash trim). Test for power at the blower connector: power present but no fan means a bad motor; no power means a bad resistor (or relay/connector). Inspect and clean corroded connectors and check the relay and ground. Both repairs are inexpensive and require no programming.

rows.title: Fuel Pump / Fuel System Failure Causing Stalling and No-Start
rows.howToFix: Test fuel pressure to confirm; replace the in-tank fuel pump module if pressure is low and replace the fuel filter (recommended every ~30,000 miles to prevent overstressing the pump). Inspect and repair any corroded fuel-tank harness connectors. Rule out the fuel pump relay and crankshaft position sensor for intermittent stalling.

Inspect and repair any corroded fuel-tank harness connectors.

rows.title: Instrument Cluster / Speedometer Stepper Motor Failure
rows.howToFix: Send the cluster to a specialist (or DIY) to replace all gauge stepper motors with new Switec 27x.168 units and re-flow the solder joints. Because mileage is stored in the cluster, repair the existing unit rather than swapping in a used cluster from another vehicle, which would import the donor's mileage.

rows.title: Aftermarket Dorman Steering Knuckle Recall (Loss of Steering Control)
rows.howToFix: If the installed knuckle could be an affected aftermarket unit, avoid driving until a qualified shop identifies both sides by part marking, material and repair history and checks for damage. Contact Dorman and use NHTSA recall 09E005 to confirm whether the installed part remains covered and what remedy and labor reimbursement are currently available; do not assume a 2009 hotline or no-charge remedy is unchanged today. Do not buy a generic knuckle from this page; installed-part identity, side, current replacement number and VIN fitment must be verified first.

rows.title: Convertible top water leaks into trunk and around rear window
rows.howToFix: Reseal or replace the buttress-pin grommets and the trunk-lid cable hose, and clear/route the top's drainage. If the top won't stow or seal, readjust or reconnect the drive-link socket on the convertible top arm. Keep the trunk weatherstrip and rear deck seals in good condition.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Ignition switch can move out of "run," stalling the engine
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN and completion history for NHTSA 14V047 with NHTSA and a GM dealer. Until applicability and completion are confirmed, minimize key-ring weight and stop using a switch that moves unexpectedly; if the engine shuts off, steer and brake deliberately to a safe stop. Ask the dealer to confirm the currently available remedy and any charge rather than relying on the 2014 owner letter. Do not buy an ignition switch, cylinder or key set from this page; campaign applicability, prior repair, part number, programming and VIN fitment must be verified first.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Check the VIN and completion history for NHTSA 14V047 with NHTSA and a GM dealer.
Ask the dealer to confirm the currently available remedy and any charge rather than relying on the 2014 owner letter.

rows.title: No interior trunk release - trunk becomes impossible to open with a dead battery
rows.howToFix: Restore power by connecting jumper cables or a charger to the underhood remote terminals to operate the release, or use the emergency procedure: remove the left rear wheel and wheelhouse liner, remove the pressure-relief valve, reach in and pull the child-safety release cable to unlatch the deck. Worn fob membranes can be replaced cheaply.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Passenger airbag suppression (PPS) sensor mat fails, disabling passenger airbag
rows.howToFix: Do not place an adult passenger in the seat when the airbag-off indicator or Service Airbag warning shows an active PPS fault. Check the VIN and recall-completion history for 17V061 with NHTSA and a GM dealer. Ask the dealer to confirm the currently available inspection/remedy and any charge; prior temporary repair did not necessarily close the recall. Do not buy a sensor mat, PPS module, reinforcement or seat part from this page; campaign applicability, diagnostic state, part number, programming and VIN fitment must be verified first.

rows.title: Rear differential/driveline clunk and gear whine
rows.howToFix: GM issued TSBs covering the noise; the common fix for chatter-on-turns is a differential fluid drain and refill with the correct limited-slip additive (owners frequently use Royal Purple or a synthetic with friction modifier). Later cars received the driveline alignment redesign.
rows.dispositionReason: The remedy is a service, tool, consumable, or fluid procedure rather than a repair part.

rows.title: "Reduced Engine Power" limp mode from throttle body coking / TAC faults
rows.howToFix: Clean (or replace) the throttle body, clean the MAF, and service the notorious driver-side engine ground strap and battery. A battery disconnect/relearn often clears the fault after cleaning. Persistent faults may require throttle body or pedal-position sensor replacement.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: Solstice Trunk Leak with Top Down (Kappa Platform)
rows.howToFix: Inspect trunk seal annually; replace if cracked ($60-$120 part). 3M weatherstrip adhesive helps reseal. Always check spare tire well after heavy rain. Some owners install a small bilge-pump style drain. Permanent fix is to confirm rain gutters at the top stowage area aren't clogged.

rows.howToFix: Diagnose fuel-rail pressure and replace the high-pressure fuel pump; the pump follower/cam lobe should also be inspected. Owners report total cost is typically several hundred to about $1,200 including labor.

rows.title: Timing chain and balance shaft chain stretch on the GXP 2.0T (LNF)
rows.howToFix: Replace the complete timing chain kit along with the balance-shaft chain kit, guides, tensioner, and water pump together since the labor overlaps. Addressing chain noise promptly prevents catastrophic interference-engine damage.

rows.title: Sunfire 2.2L Ecotec (L61) Head Gasket / Head Crack
rows.howToFix: Pressure-test cooling system to confirm. Head gasket replacement ~$1,000-$1,800 — but ALWAYS have the head pressure-tested and resurfaced (~$150-$250 machine shop) since cracking is so common. If head is cracked, a used head is often the most economical replacement ($200-$400 from yard). Driving while overheating destroys the head; tow it.

rows.title: T-top and roof weatherstrip leaks
rows.howToFix: Replace the T-top and roof-rail weatherstripping with new reproduction seals (widely available from F-body/Firebird specialists), clean and re-seat the moldings, verify the T-top panels are properly adjusted/latched, and confirm the roof drain channels are clear.

rows.title: LT1 Optispark distributor failure from moisture and ozone contamination
rows.howToFix: Replace the Optispark with a vented-style unit (AC Delco or a quality aftermarket), replace the water pump at the same time since it must come off for access, and route a small hose from the water pump weep hole to divert coolant away from the distributor. Keep the engine bay dry and avoid pressure-washing near the front of the engine. Replacing plug wires while it is apart is standard practice.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: LT1 water pump failure (shaft bearing/seal) with weep-hole coolant leak onto Optispark
rows.howToFix: Replace the water pump (AC Delco or quality aftermarket) and, given the shared labor to remove the belt, crank pulley, and access area, replace the Optispark at the same time. Add a diverter hose on the weep hole to protect the distributor. Inspect the drive seal behind the pump.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Inspect the drive seal behind the pump.

rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Pop-up headlight motor nylon gear stripping (4th-gen)
rows.howToFix: Rebuild the original motor with an aftermarket brass or aluminum gear kit (both motors typically done together). As a temporary fix a stripped nylon gear can be rotated 180 degrees to expose good teeth. Re-secure the motor housing to prevent repeat failure.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: 4L60E automatic transmission 3-4 clutch pack failure
rows.howToFix: Rebuild the transmission with an upgraded 3-4 clutch pack (Raybestos GPZ or Borg-Warner Hi-Energy frictions are the community favorites), remove the problematic load-release springs, add a shift/valve-body correction kit and a stronger backing plate, and use fresh fluid and filter. Keeping the trans cool with an auxiliary cooler and servicing fluid on schedule extends life.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Early LS1 piston slap and high oil consumption
rows.howToFix: Cold-start piston slap that quiets when warm is generally considered cosmetic and can be monitored rather than repaired. For genuine excessive oil consumption, GM released updated higher-tension oil rings and a Napier second compression ring; severe cases require a ring job or short-block replacement. Regular oil-level checks and using the correct oil weight are the practical mitigations.

rows.title: Vibe 1.8L (1ZZ-FE) Oil Consumption — Coked Piston Rings
rows.howToFix: Top-end engine cleaner (BG EPR, AMSOIL Engine and Transmission Flush) cycled through oil changes can sometimes free stuck rings. Failing that, piston-ring replacement (~$1,800-$3,000) or full short-block swap (~$3,000-$4,500). Monitor oil level weekly until consumption rate is known. Switching to a high-mileage oil (Mobil 1 High Mileage 5W-30) sometimes slows the rate of consumption.

rows.title: EVAP System Faults — Charcoal Canister and Vent VSV Failure (P0440/P0441/P0446)
rows.howToFix: First rule out a loose or worn gas cap, then test the vent VSV and replace it if stuck (a much cheaper repair than the full canister); replace the charcoal canister assembly if it is saturated or its integrated valves have failed. Stop topping off the tank after the nozzle clicks to avoid saturating the new canister.

rows.title: Front Door Glass Bolts Loosen — Window Binds and Shatters (Recall 08V-162)
rows.howToFix: If a front window rattles, binds or shifts in the channel, stop operating it and keep hands clear of the glass. Check the VIN under campaign 08V-162/GM 07273 and contact an authorized GM dealer to confirm whether it is open and the current bolt inspection/replacement availability and charge. If glass has separated or shattered, secure the opening and use a qualified repairer. Do not buy bolts, a regulator or glass from this page; power-window equipment, affected side, damage, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

If a 2003-2004 Vibe has an open Takata recall covered by the Do Not Drive warning, do not drive it; contact GM to arrange the current authorized remedy and ask about mobile repair or towing. For any open 2009-2010 inflator campaign, schedule the authorized remedy promptly. Confirm current availability and charge when scheduling. Do not buy or handle an inflator or airbag module from this page; campaign, VIN and repair history determine the remedy.

rows.title: ECM Circuit Board Solder Cracks Causing Stalling and No-Start (Recall 10V-387)
rows.howToFix: If the engine stalls in traffic, move out of the travel lane if possible and arrange towing rather than repeatedly driving it. Check the VIN and ECM production number under campaign 10V-387/GM 10282; contact an authorized GM dealer to confirm the recall is open and the current inspection/replacement availability and charge before service. Outside an open campaign, verify power, grounds, network communication, codes, production number and programming requirements before replacing the ECM. Do not buy an ECM from this page; production number, programming, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.howToFix: Replace the pistons and rings with the updated Toyota design (the ZE7-style repair), or install a replacement engine in severe cases. In the interim, check oil every fuel fill-up and top off to prevent bearing damage.

rows.title: Power Window Master Switch Overheats and Melts — Fire Risk (Recalls 12V-491 / 15V-689)
rows.howToFix: If the switch is hot, smells burned, smokes or shows melting, stop using it, turn the vehicle off when safe, move occupants away and call emergency services if fire is present. Check the VIN under 12V-491 and 15V-689 and contact an authorized GM dealer to confirm open status and current inspection/lubrication or circuit-board replacement availability and charge. Do not apply household or unapproved lubricant. Do not buy a switch from this page; campaign status, heat damage, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: Unintended Acceleration — Sticking Accelerator Pedal and Floor Mat Entrapment (Recall 10V-024)
rows.howToFix: Have a GM or Toyota dealer perform the recall remedies free of charge: a reinforcement bar installed in the pedal assembly (or pedal replacement) for the sticky-pedal defect, plus the floor mat interference remedy. Verify completion via a NHTSA VIN recall lookup and never stack aftermarket floor mats.
